symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of observed vertices.

symbols.name: I_n
symbols.def: The identity matrix of order \(n\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The directed support of the structural coefficient matrix.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The support of off-diagonal disturbance covariances.

symbols.name: pa_G
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)=\{u\in V_n:u\to v\in D\}\).

symbols.name: Lambda
symbols.def: \(\Lambda_{uv}=\lambda_{uv}\) for \(u\to v\in D\) and \(\Lambda_{uv}=0\) otherwise.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: A symmetric disturbance covariance matrix before its support and positivity conditions are imposed.

symbols.name: theta_G
symbols.def: \(\theta_G=(\lambda_{uv}:u\to v\in D;\ \omega_{uv}:u=v\text{ or }u\leftrightarrow v\in B)\).

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: \(\Sigma=(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\Sigma)\).

symbols.name: phi_G
symbols.def: The polynomial map induced by \(\Sigma=(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\) after fixing every missing off-diagonal disturbance entry to zero; acyclicity makes the inverse matrices finite path sums.

symbols.name: tau_G
symbols.def: The homomorphism that fixes every coordinate of \(\theta_G\) and sends \(s\) to \(\phi_G(\theta_G)\).

symbols.name: I_G
symbols.def: \(I_G=\ker(\tau_G)\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: A structural or disturbance parameter to be identified.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: The source coordinates available before identifying \(q\).

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: A total polynomial-degree cutoff.

symbols.name: A_d
symbols.def: \(A_d(S)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\tau_G(u):u\text{ is a monomial in }S\cup s,\ \deg u\le d\}\).

symbols.name: C_d
symbols.def: \(C_d(S)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\tau_G(u):u\text{ is a monomial in }S\cup s,\ \deg u\le d-1\}\).

symbols.name: Cl_d
symbols.def: Starting from the empty set, repeatedly adjoin every \(q\) for which \(A_d(S)\cap qC_d(S)\ne\{0\}\), and stop at the least fixed point.

symbols.name: Reach_d
symbols.def: The collection of source-coordinate sets obtainable from the empty set by successively adjoining a coordinate with a degree-\(d\) recursive certificate over coordinates already adjoined.

symbols.name: ID_G
symbols.def: The minimum, over all identifying orders of every coordinate in \(\theta_G\), of the largest total degree of a certificate \(q a(S,s)-b(S,s)\in I_G\) with nonzero denominator on the model.

symbols.name: s_HMS
symbols.def: \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}\) is the maximum directed indegree in Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2--7.4; the proposal uses their specialization \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\). Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for the auxiliary-cutset subclass.

symbols.name: HTCcert
symbols.def: The indicator that \(G\) is certified by the recursive half-trek criterion of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton.

symbols.name: ICcert
symbols.def: The indicator that \(G\) is certified by recursive instrumental cutsets in the sense of Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: ACcert
symbols.def: The indicator that \(G\) is certified by recursive auxiliary cutsets in the sense of Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: The common length of the two missing-bidirected cycles in the two-parent windmill gadget.

symbols.name: W2_ell
symbols.def: The explicit graph constructed in \(\mathrm{def:two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}windmill}\).

symbols.name: zeta_ell
symbols.def: \(\zeta_{\ell}=\lambda_{\ell-1,\ell+1}\), the coefficient on the central skip edge of \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\).

symbols.name: Hrank
symbols.def: For the multiplication map \(m_{\zeta,S}:C_d(S)\to\bigl(A_d(S)+\zeta_{\ell}C_d(S)\bigr)/A_d(S)\), \(c\mapsto\zeta_{\ell}c+A_d(S)\), let \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) be the sum of squares of all \(\dim C_d(S)\)-square minors of a rational matrix for \(m_{\zeta,S}\); it is nonzero exactly when multiplication by \(\zeta_{\ell}\) is injective modulo \(A_d(S)\), equivalently when no degree-\(d\) certificate can adjoin \(\zeta_{\ell}\) after \(S\).

symbols.name: G2rat_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) is the class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\).

symbols.name: D2
symbols.def: \(D_2(n)=\max_{G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)}ID_G\).

symbols.name: f_2
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) as the scale of \(D_2(n)\).

symbols.name: c_2
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

symbols.name: C_2
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

symbols.name: n_0
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) as the first size at which the matching asymptotic inequalities hold.

symbols.name: Gstar_n
symbols.def: For \(n\ge6\), \(G_n^{\star}\) is \(W_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}^{(2)}\) plus \(n-2\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) isolated vertices.

symbols.name: K6
symbols.def: The chain \(1\to2\to3\to4\to5\to6\) with all bidirected edges except \(\{2,3\},\{2,4\},\{3,4\},\{4,5\},\{4,6\},\{5,6\}\).

symbols.name: FrontierHandle
symbols.def: Start the lower direction from the explicit two-parent windmills \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\). At \(W_3^{(2)}\) and degree \(d=4\), first compute reduced rational formulas for every structural and disturbance coordinate, exhaustive half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset failure transcripts, and the exact monomial-basis matrix of \(m_{\zeta,S}\) with a displayed nonzero \(\dim C_4(S)\)-square minor for every \(S\in\operatorname{Reach}_4(W_3^{(2)})\) not containing \(\zeta_3\). Lift this audited instance to every \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) by proving generic birationality and \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\ne0\) for the locked coordinate \(\zeta_{\ell}\) for every set \(S\) obtainable before \(\zeta_{\ell}\) by degree-\(d\) recursive adjunctions of any structural or disturbance coordinates. For the upper direction, control recursive elimination by mixed-component decomposition and the multigraded graph algebra of \(\phi_G\), and prove that its Hilbert bounds dominate the same recursive filtration.

symbols.name: B2
symbols.def: Conditional on completion of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\), \(B_2(n)=\max\{\lceil C_2 f_2(n)\rceil,D_2(1),\ldots,D_2(n_0-1)\}\), with the finite exceptional values derived there by exact closure.

symbols.name: DBI
symbols.def: The weighted-homogeneous adaptive-ordering algorithm of Hollering, Misra, and Sturma run once at input degree \(B_2(n)\), without a wall-clock timeout and with exact certificates retained.

symbols.name: alpha_alg
symbols.def: A constant such that square matrix row reduction uses \(O(m^{\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}})\) arithmetic operations.

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.def: The structural-equation disturbance with covariance \(\Omega\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The solution of \(X=\Lambda^{\mathsf T}X+\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: The number of independent observational units.

symbols.name: X_i
symbols.def: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are copies of \(X\).

symbols.name: Sigma_hat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Sigma=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N(X_i-\bar X)(X_i-\bar X)^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r=|\theta_G|\), the fixed number of returned structural and disturbance coordinates.

symbols.name: P_F
symbols.def: \(P_F=(P_{F,1},\ldots,P_{F,r})\) is the numerator family in the reduced rational output.

symbols.name: Q_F
symbols.def: \(Q_F=(Q_{F,1},\ldots,Q_{F,r})\) is the nonzero denominator family in the reduced rational output.

symbols.name: F_G
symbols.def: \(F_G(s)=(P_{F,j}(s)/Q_{F,j}(s))_{j=1}^r\) is a deterministic vector of reduced rational formulas returned by \(DBI\) for graph \(G\).

symbols.name: J_F
symbols.type: Jacobian of the returned rational map

symbols.name: IF_F
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{IF}_F(X)=J_F(s)\operatorname{vech}(XX^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma)\).

symbols.name: V_F
symbols.def: \(V_F=\mathbb E[\operatorname{IF}_F(X)\operatorname{IF}_F(X)^{\mathsf T}]\).

symbols.name: Vhat_F
symbols.def: On \(\min_j|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|>0\), \(\widehat V_F\) is the empirical second moment of the influence vector with \(s\), \(J_F\), and \(\Sigma\) replaced by their sample analogues; at a denominator pole it is defined to be the zero matrix.

symbols.name: theta_hat_G
symbols.def: The finite-sample convention sets \(F_G(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)=0_r\) when any returned denominator vanishes. Thus \(\widehat\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)\) when \(\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|>0\), and \(\widehat\theta_G=0_r\) at a denominator pole.

symbols.name: delta_chart
symbols.def: A fixed positive chart constant.

symbols.name: kappa_chart
symbols.def: A fixed positive chart constant.

symbols.name: K_chart
symbols.def: A fixed finite chart constant.

symbols.name: nu_chart
symbols.def: A fixed positive chart constant.

symbols.name: Chart
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\) is the class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}chart}\).

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: The desired simultaneous Wald noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: Wald_G
symbols.def: If \(\min_j|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|=0\) or \(\widehat V_F\) is singular, define \(\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)=\mathbb R^r\). Otherwise define \(\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)=\{t\in\mathbb R^r:N(\widehat\theta_G-t)^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_F^{-1}(\widehat\theta_G-t)\le\chi^2_{r,1-\gamma}\}\).

standard.name: bounded directed indegree, specialized to two

assumptions.condition: The parametrization \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.
\(\Omega_{uv}=0\) for every distinct \(u,v\in V_n\) with \(u\leftrightarrow v\notin B\).
\(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent and identically distributed as \(X\).

novel.justification: Every fixed covariance strictly inside a reduced rational chart satisfies such a margin on a sufficiently small compact neighborhood; the condition excludes poles that make the structural inverse empirically unstable.

standard.name: uniform positive definiteness on a compact parametric chart

novel.justification: The condition holds on compact neighborhoods of regular covariance points where the selected structural coordinates have linearly independent first-order fluctuations; it separates ordinary Wald behavior from singular charts.

definitions.name: rationally identifiable indegree-two graph class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)=\{G=(V_n,D,B):(V_n,D)\text{ is acyclic},\ \max_{v\in V_n}|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|\le2,\ \phi_G\text{ is generically birational onto its image}\}\).

definitions.name: degree-bounded recursive certificate
definitions.construction: For \(q\notin S\), a certificate at degree \(d\) is \(q a(S,s)-b(S,s)\in I_G\) with \(\deg\{q a-b\}\le d\) and \(a\) nonzero in the model coordinate ring.

definitions.name: rank-intersection spans
definitions.construction: \(A_d(S)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\tau_G(u):u\text{ is a monomial in }S\cup s,\deg u\le d\}\) and \(C_d(S)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\tau_G(u):u\text{ is a monomial in }S\cup s,\deg u\le d-1\}\).

definitions.name: two-parent windmill gadget
definitions.construction: For \(\ell\ge3\), \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) has vertex set \(V_{2\ell}\), directed edges \(i\to i+1\) for \(1\le i<2\ell\) and \(i\to i+2\) for \(1\le i\le2\ell-2\), and every bidirected edge except \[\{\{i,i+1\}:2\le i\le\ell\}\cup\{\{\ell+1,2\}\}\cup\{\{i,i+1\}:\ell+1\le i\le2\ell-1\}\cup\{\{2\ell,\ell+1\}\}.\] Thus the missing-bidirected graph on the nonroot vertices consists of two \(\ell\)-cycles meeting only at vertex \(\ell+1\), and the directed indegree equals two from vertex \(3\) onward.

definitions.name: locked-coordinate Hilbert-rank obstruction
definitions.construction: For \(S\subseteq\theta_{W_{\ell}^{(2)}}\setminus\{\zeta_{\ell}\}\), form \(m_{\zeta,S}:C_d(S)\to\bigl(A_d(S)+\zeta_{\ell}C_d(S)\bigr)/A_d(S)\), \(c\mapsto\zeta_{\ell}c+A_d(S)\), in exact monomial-image bases. Define \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) as the sum of squares of all \(\dim C_d(S)\)-square minors of this matrix. Then \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\ne0\) exactly when \(A_d(S)\cap\zeta_{\ell}C_d(S)=\{0\}\).

definitions.name: intrinsic recursive-frontier handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\) to the windmill family by proving \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\ne0\) for every degree-\(d\) recursively reachable \(S\subseteq\theta_{W_{\ell}^{(2)}}\setminus\{\zeta_{\ell}\}\), including sets containing disturbance coordinates, and compare the resulting lower scale with the graph-uniform Hilbert bound from the multigraded graph algebra of \(\phi_G\).

definitions.name: two-triangle early-kill graph
definitions.construction: \(K_6\) has directed edges \(i\to i+1\) for \(i=1,\ldots,5\) and has every bidirected edge except the six pairs \(\{2,3\},\{2,4\},\{3,4\},\{4,5\},\{4,6\},\{5,6\}\).

definitions.name: frontier-conditional total degree schedule
definitions.construction: Conditional on a proof of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\), compute \(B_2(n)=\max\{\lceil C_2f_2(n)\rceil,D_2(1),\ldots,D_2(n_0-1)\}\), run \(DBI\) once through its complete internal weighted-degree loop at cutoff \(B_2(n)\), disable finite timeouts, and return exact identifying formulas or the complete negative certificate.

definitions.name: rational plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: If \(\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|>0\), set \(\widehat\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)\) and obtain \(\widehat V_F\) by empirical averaging of the plug-in influence vectors. If any \(Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)=0\), adopt the explicit sample-evaluation convention \(F_G(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)=\widehat\theta_G=0_r\) and \(\widehat V_F=0_{r\times r}\).

definitions.name: simultaneous Wald set
definitions.construction: If \(\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|=0\) or \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat V_F)=0\), set \(\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)=\mathbb R^r\). On the complementary event, set \(\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)=\{t\in\mathbb R^r:N(\widehat\theta_G-t)^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_F^{-1}(\widehat\theta_G-t)\le\chi^2_{r,1-\gamma}\}\).

statements.statement: For every acyclic mixed graph \(G\), every \(d\ge1\), and the full original source vector \(\theta_G\), \(ID_G\le d\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Cl}_d(G)=\theta_G\). The closure stabilizes after at most \(|\theta_G|\) strict rounds, and a proper fixed point is a certificate against every recursive order, including orders that identify disturbance covariances before structural coefficients.
statements.justification: The equivalence supplies the order-free object on which both sides of the frontier can be proved.
statements.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma minimize over recursive identifying orders, but do not give a least-fixed-point rank characterization that can certify lower bounds simultaneously over all orders and all original parameters.
statements.consumer: The lower-bound argument obtains a finite exact certificate that cannot be invalidated by a structural- or error-parameter shortcut.

statements.statement: Among all \(64\) topologically labelled three-vertex acyclic mixed graphs, exactly eight have \(ID_G=1\), twenty-one have \(ID_G=2\), two have \(ID_G=3\), and thirty-three have positive-dimensional generic fibers. Consequently \(D_2(1)=1\), \(D_2(2)=2\), \(D_2(3)=3\), and \(D_2(n)\ge3\) for every \(n\ge3\) by isolated-vertex padding.
statements.justification: The exact base case validates the source degree convention and exposes error variances as load-bearing coordinates.
statements.gap: Published small-graph censuses classify rational or generic identification, not the minimum recursive certificate degree over structural and disturbance coordinates.
statements.consumer: The frontier recurrence and every implementation receive exact base cases and analytic regression tests.

statements.statement: For the exact worked instance \(W_3^{(2)}\), supply a reduced rational identifying formula and graph-ideal certificate for every \(q\in\theta_{W_3^{(2)}}\); an exhaustive half-trek witness, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset search transcript proving \(\operatorname{HTCcert}(W_3^{(2)})=\operatorname{ICcert}(W_3^{(2)})=\operatorname{ACcert}(W_3^{(2)})=0\); and, for every \(S\in\operatorname{Reach}_4(W_3^{(2)})\) with \(\zeta_3\notin S\), the exact monomial-basis matrix of \(m_{\zeta,S}:C_4(S)\to(A_4(S)+\zeta_3C_4(S))/A_4(S)\), its rank, and a displayed nonzero \(\dim C_4(S)\)-square minor. Then prove for every \(\ell\ge3\) that \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) is generically birational onto its covariance image and that \[\operatorname{HTCcert}(W_{\ell}^{(2)})=\operatorname{ICcert}(W_{\ell}^{(2)})=\operatorname{ACcert}(W_{\ell}^{(2)})=0.\] Supply rational identifying formulas or exact graph-ideal certificates for all coordinates and complete failure transcripts for all three criteria. Consequently the family lies in \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(2\ell)\) and strictly separates rational identification at directed indegree two from the bounded half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset subclasses, in particular from auxiliary cutsets.
statements.justification: A lower-bound family must first be shown to inhabit the unclassified portion of the rationally identifiable indegree-two class.
statements.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Proposition 7.4 gives the auxiliary-cutset bound \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), hence \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\), but does not show that auxiliary cutsets exhaust rational identification at this indegree.
statements.consumer: The sharp-frontier lower bound receives an explicit legal family that cannot inherit a bounded certificate from any of the three published subclass guarantees.

statements.statement: Using exact rational rank intersections over every coordinate of \(\theta_{K_6}\), determine whether \(\operatorname{Cl}_4(K_6)=\theta_{K_6}\). If equality holds, certify the complete closure transcript and reject cycle length alone as evidence of degree growth; if it fails, return a proper fixed point and use its surviving multigrading to calibrate the windmill obstruction in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).
statements.justification: This bounded computation destroys the most tempting false growth heuristic before the asymptotic family is frozen.
statements.gap: Tree-cycle papers prove sound quadratic elimination, but neither they nor the degree-bounded algorithm compute the source-defined minimum degree for this outside-HTC two-cycle graph.
statements.consumer: The windmill program receives either a concrete low-degree multigrading or an immediate warning that two-cycle length cannot support its lower exponent.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\), determine a positive scale \(f_2(n)\), constants \(0<c_2\le C_2<\infty\), and an onset \(n_0\) such that the padded windmills satisfy \(G_n^{\star}\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), \(\operatorname{HTCcert}(G_n^{\star})=\operatorname{ICcert}(G_n^{\star})=\operatorname{ACcert}(G_n^{\star})=0\), and, for every \(n\ge n_0\), \[c_2f_2(n)\le ID_{G_n^{\star}}\le D_2(n)\le C_2f_2(n).\] Determine the finite exceptional values \(D_2(1),\ldots,D_2(n_0-1)\) by exact closure. The upper direction must show that a proper closure at degree \(\lceil C_2f_2(n)\rceil\) forces failure of generic birationality. For the lower direction, for every \(S\in\operatorname{Reach}_{\lfloor c_2f_2(n)\rfloor-1}(G_n^{\star})\) with \(\zeta_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\notin S\), prove \(\mathfrak H_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lfloor c_2f_2(n)\rfloor-1}(S)\ne0\). This exact Hilbert-rank obstruction must survive every permitted earlier adjunction of structural or disturbance coordinates and hence keep \(\zeta_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\) outside \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\lfloor c_2f_2(n)\rfloor-1}(G_n^{\star})\). Solving both directions strictly strengthens the prespecified-degree guarantee of Hollering, Misra, and Sturma on the full class \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), rather than reproving their bounded subclass results.
statements.justification: The matching scale is the first graph-uniform calibration of minimum recursive formula degree at the first non-tree indegree.
statements.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma require an external degree input for the full rationally identifiable class. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, while Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets; at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\) these are \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\). Tree identification controls scalar Möbius cycles, and inverse-map regularity theory does not align its degree with recursive SEM certificates.
statements.consumer: The degree-bounded symbolic algorithm receives a necessary-order stopping threshold rather than an analyst-chosen promise parameter.

statements.statement: Conditional on a proof of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) and hence on a proved uniform cutoff \(B_2(n)\), let \(G\) be any acyclic indegree-two mixed graph on \(n\) vertices. One exact call to \(DBI\) at degree \(B_2(n)\) terminates and returns yes with minimum-degree rational formulas if and only if \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\). Its arithmetic complexity is \[O\!\left(B_2(n)n^5\{3B_2(n)n\}^{4\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}B_2(n)^2\log(3B_2(n)n)}\right),\] and a no answer is accompanied by a complete exact bounded-search certificate rather than a timeout status. No unconditional total schedule is asserted before the frontier is proved.
statements.justification: Once established, the frontier converts a promise search into a total formula-producing decision procedure on the stated class.
statements.gap: Dörfler et al. give a total polynomial-space generic-identification decision without formulas, while Hollering, Misra, and Sturma return formulas only relative to a supplied cutoff.
statements.consumer: Users of DegBoundedIdentifiability obtain an auditable stopping rule and an explicit worst-case resource bound for indegree-two graphs.

statements.statement: Fix \(n\), \(G\), \(r\), and a deterministic returned map \(F_G\), and use the total pole and singular-covariance conventions in \(\mathrm{def:plug\mbox{-}in\mbox{-}estimator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}set}\). Uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\), \[\sqrt N\{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,V_F),\qquad \widehat V_F\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}V_F.\] Moreover, \[\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\!\left\{\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|=0\right\}\to0,\qquad \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\widehat V_F\text{ is singular}\}\to0.\] Consequently \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{F_G(s)\in\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)\}\to1-\gamma\). The result covers every fixed finite vector of rational formulas returned by the total schedule on the Gaussian submodel; it makes no efficiency claim.
statements.justification: A symbolic inverse becomes empirically usable only after its full joint first-order law and simultaneous coverage are supplied.
statements.gap: Mareis, Sturma, and Drton treat fixed half-trek estimators, whereas the returned map here may be any deterministic rational quotient produced by degree-bounded elimination; Drton and Xiao show why the nondegeneracy boundary cannot be ignored.
statements.consumer: An analyst can report simultaneous confidence regions for all structural coefficients returned by the exact stopping schedule on a declared regular chart.

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a fixed acyclic linear Gaussian structural equation model.
sampling_model.units: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent copies of the observed \(n\)-vector.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the full supported structural mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; regularity is stated through covariance, rational-denominator, and influence-covariance margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(\Sigma\) by \(\widehat\Sigma\), differentiate the deterministic rational output \(F_G\), and estimate the joint influence covariance by empirical plug-in averaging. At a sample denominator pole use the zero evaluation convention; at a pole or singular \(\widehat V_F\), return \(\mathbb R^r\) as the confidence set.

estimand_functional: \(\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\Sigma)\), with minimum recursive certificate degree \(ID_G\) and graph-uniform frontier \(D_2(n)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For prespecified \(d\ge ID_G\), the degree-bounded algorithm returns minimum-degree formulas; Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 bound half-trek and instrumental-cutset certificates by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 bounds auxiliary-cutset certificates by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), yielding \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\).
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for rational identification by recursive linear systems.
Instrumental cutsets give a sound graphical identification criterion for linear structural causal models.
Auxiliary cutsets enlarge the efficiently certifiable subclass by recursively using identified coefficients as auxiliary information.
A missing cycle in a directed-tree model yields a quadratic equation, and multiple cycles can select one rational root.
Every directed-tree structural coefficient is generically one-identifiable, two-identifiable, or unidentifiable, and the classification is complete.
The complete tree-only identification predicate can be implemented in randomized \(O(n^3\log^2n)\) time.
A Cohen--Macaulay graph or Rees algebra yields inverse-degree bounds through regularity and Jacobian-dual minors.
Generic identification in unrestricted linear structural causal models has a sound and complete polynomial-space decision procedure.
Fixed half-trek estimators have recursive influence functions, asymptotic normality, and plug-in Wald inference.
Bow-free path recovery is stable under quantitative conditions, while a four-node example has unbounded condition number.
At a vanishing constraint gradient, the Wald statistic can converge to a nonstandard rational function of a Gaussian vector.

tldr: The field-level target is the sharp recursive degree frontier \(D_2(n)\) over every structural and disturbance coordinate and every identifying order. The lower program starts from the explicit two-parent windmills, requires an audited \(W_3^{(2)}\) instance with rational formulas, exhaustive half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset failure transcripts, and exact degree-four rank-obstruction matrices for every reachable predecessor set, and then lifts the substitution-robust obstruction to the family; the upper program matches that scale through the multigraded covariance-map algebra. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give the bound \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\); the resulting \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) bounds at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\) are cited background. Only after the uniform frontier is proved is it compiled into a total formula-returning schedule; its fixed rational output is evaluated with an explicit pole convention and yields a Wald set that is the full parameter space on pole or singular covariance events, which vanish uniformly on regular charts.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's algorithm is complete only relative to a supplied degree. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets, specializing to \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\). No theorem calibrates minimum recursive degree over all rationally identifiable indegree-two graphs or exhibits an explicit family outside auxiliary cutsets with an order-robust lower invariant.
project_justification.niche: Directed indegree two is the first sparse class in which a missing covariance equation can couple four structural coefficients. The explicit windmill family isolates this block interaction while retaining an exact rank-intersection filtration that includes disturbance-coordinate shortcuts.
project_justification.fill: The central open-ended question proves matching bounds for \(D_2(n)\), establishes the padded two-parent windmills as a rationally identifiable family outside all three bounded graphical subclasses, and lower-bounds them with \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) over every degree-reachable predecessor set. The mandatory \(W_3^{(2)}\) audit supplies coordinate formulas, three complete criterion-failure transcripts, and every degree-four obstruction matrix before the family induction. The resulting cutoff is compiled conditionally into exact formula output and total finite-sample fixed-chart inference.

related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and identify structural degree growth as the missing complexity input. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give the half-trek and instrumental-cutset bounds \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), while Proposition 7.4 gives the auxiliary-cutset bound \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\); at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\), these are \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\). These results are cited background. The sharp-frontier question strictly tightens their prespecified-degree guarantee only on the full rationally identifiable indegree-two class. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton supply the half-trek linear-system baseline. Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim introduce instrumental cutsets, while Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim introduce auxiliary cutsets; the worked \(W_3^{(2)}\) instance and the full windmill family require exhaustive failure transcripts for all three criteria. Van der Zander et al. derive the bilinear missing-cycle equations, while Gupta and Bläser prove the complete tree-only one, two, or infinite classification and Briefs and Bläser accelerate that predicate; these papers inform the degree-four kill test rather than serve as frontier targets. Hassanzadeh and Simis motivate Hilbert control of birational inverse degree, but their hypotheses are not assumed for SEM covariance maps. Dörfler et al. provide the total decision benchmark without formula output. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton inform fixed-chart inference for deterministic rational output; Sankararaman, Louis, and Goyal motivate quantitative conditioning, and Drton and Xiao delimit the singular Wald boundary. The finite-sample construction therefore assigns the full ambient parameter space at denominator poles or singular plug-in covariance matrices and proves both exceptional events vanish uniformly on the fixed chart.
technical_internal_limitation: The six-vertex two-triangle construction supplies only a rational certificate of degree at most nine and does not establish \(ID_{K_6}>4\). The two-parent windmills are explicit candidate gadgets, but even the required \(W_3^{(2)}\) formulas, three criterion-failure transcripts, and degree-four rank-obstruction matrices are open deliverables rather than presolved facts. The upper Hilbert comparison must be proved for the SEM recursive filtration; no Cohen--Macaulay property or equality with projective inverse degree is assumed.
honest_scope: The field-level contribution is the open-ended two-sided frontier together with its explicit outside-auxiliary-cutset windmill family and substitution-robust Hilbert-rank lower invariant. The closure equivalence, three-vertex census, exact \(W_3^{(2)}\) audit, windmill separation, matching scale, and fixed-chart inferential extension are claims to prove. The degree-four computation is a falsification gate. The total stopping schedule is explicitly conditional on a proved uniform frontier and has no unconditional force before that result. The inference theorem is fixed-dimensional and regular-chart; its estimator is set to zero at a sample denominator pole, its Wald set is the full ambient space at a pole or singular \(\widehat V_F\), and both exceptional events must vanish uniformly. No semiparametric efficiency, adaptive formula-selection validity, growing-dimension Gaussian approximation, or singular-chart coverage is claimed. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), hence \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\); the exact base case is \(D_2(3)=3\).

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Definition of \(ID_G\); Corollary 4.5; Theorem 5.1; Conclusion, final paragraph
seed_details.opportunity: Determine the sharp asymptotic scale of \(D_2(n)\) and match it with the explicit two-parent windmills outside the auxiliary-cutset subclass.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the supplied cutoff in Theorem 5.1 by a graph-uniform closure theorem, prove generic birationality and auxiliary-cutset failure for \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\), and establish nonvanishing of \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) for every degree-reachable predecessor set of the locked coordinate.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches pairing acyclic indegree two with recursive certificate degree, birational inverse degree, and graph-uniform rational identification found bounded-degree search, general inverse-map bounds, and tree-only cycle algorithms, but no occupied frontier theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say bounded indegree makes the source algorithm's degree bound immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) on the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) on auxiliary cutsets, hence \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\); no completeness theorem follows for the full indegree-two class.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the minimum recursive degree over every order and all original parameters, not the degree of one expanded formula or a do-calculus effect functional.

seed_details.anchor_location: Equations (2)--(3), Composition and Elimination, Lemmas 8, 12--13, Lemma 25, and Theorem 27
seed_details.opportunity: Prove an if-and-only-if finite obstruction classification showing that one absolute degree closes every rationally identifiable indegree-two graph.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the tree proof's equation with exactly two scalar indeterminates by a complete classification of finite correspondences between two-parent coefficient blocks.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for missing-cycle completeness, two-parent bilinear block propagation, and constant-degree rational identification found only the directed-tree classification and its faster implementation.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may call this TreeID with two-vector nodes.
seed_details.rebuttal: A missing covariance equation now involves up to four structural coefficients, so Möbius propagation, the unicyclic component argument, and the two-root conclusion all fail at the first algebraic step.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The degree-four computation for \(K_6\) is a mandatory kill test; the seed is abandoned if exact closure already contradicts its finite-obstruction route.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1, Appendix A.6 pairwise elimination proof, Theorem 2, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Determine the sharp minimum recursive degree on rationally identifiable directed-tree models before enlarging the lower family to indegree two.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn the product of missing-edge Möbius matrices from an upper construction into a valuation or Newton-polytope lower bound valid over every cycle choice and disturbance-parameter substitution.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches found tree fiber-cardinality completeness and faster cycle detection, but no theorem for the minimum source-defined certificate degree as cycle length grows.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say linear expression growth follows immediately by multiplying \(2\times2\) transfer matrices.
seed_details.rebuttal: Matrix multiplication only upper-bounds one displayed certificate; the missing result is a minimum-degree lower bound over every recursive structural and error order.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a fallback lower-bound laboratory, not a claim that the indegree-two frontier equals the tree frontier.

seed_details.opportunity: Exhibit singleton generic fibers at indegree two with arbitrarily large minimum rational inverse degree, separating uniqueness from formula complexity.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the tree theorem's one, two, or infinite fiber trichotomy by an LSEM-realizable birational map whose inverse multidegree is intrinsically large.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: General birational maps with large inverse degree exist, but searches found no acyclic indegree-two covariance realization or recursive-order lower bound.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may invoke standard high-degree Cremona inverses.
seed_details.rebuttal: Arbitrary Cremona maps do not satisfy the acyclic covariance factorization, support restrictions, positive-definite chart, or recursive certificate convention.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A single tuned covariance does not count; the separation must be generic on a nonempty regular region.

seed_details.opportunity: Bound recursive identifying degree by an explicit function of the treewidth of the parameter-equation incidence graph and prove a matching realizable lower bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pathwise pair elimination by separator elimination while preserving minimum inverse degree rather than presentation degree.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Sparse-elimination and treewidth results bound intermediate systems, but searches found no recursive rational-certificate theorem for linear SEM covariance ideals.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may call the result standard sparse-elimination folklore.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard bounds concern a chosen elimination presentation; the lower match must survive alternative recursive orders and be realized by supported covariance equations.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The named focal object is a parameterized degree frontier, not generic runtime folklore.

seed_details.opportunity: Classify a strict super-class of directed trees using projective transfers between two-parent coefficient blocks.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Aggregate enough missing-covariance equations to define a generically finite projective correspondence before composing transfers.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for matrix-pencil, projective-transfer, and two-parent SEM identification found no target-method match.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say a hand-built subclass avoids the graph-uniform question.
seed_details.rebuttal: The subclass is retained only if it contains every directed tree and a genuinely two-parent outside-HTC family with a proved strict inclusion.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The inclusion relation to the published tree class is part of the deliverable.

seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 1, Theorem 5.1, implementation discussion, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Compile a valid graph-uniform bound into a terminating exact formula-returning procedure.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the user-supplied \(d\) and wall-clock timeout by a proved structural cutoff and a complete exact negative transcript.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Dörfler et al. supply a total generic-identification decision but no rational formulas; no located procedure combines totality with minimum-degree formula output on indegree two.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say the schedule is immediate once the frontier is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the mathematical kernel, so the schedule is retained only as a compiled theorem and never ranked as the proposal's independent contribution.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is explicitly downgraded from kernel status.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 7, Proposition 9, Proposition 12, Remark 8, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Among rational certificates equal on the covariance model, characterize the first-order variance-minimizing off-model representative and its efficiency frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project ambient gradients of equivalent rational representatives onto the covariance-model tangent space before optimizing the remaining normal component.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches found witness-dependent HTC variances and symbolic minimum-degree formulas, but no joint optimization of formula degree and influence variance over equivalent representatives.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say equal rational functionals necessarily have equal derivatives.
seed_details.rebuttal: Only tangential derivatives agree on the model variety; empirical covariance fluctuates in ambient normal directions, where different representatives and HTC witnesses can have different variance.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is an efficiency-bound seed, not a bare delta-method appendix.

seed_details.anchor_location: Definition 1.2, Theorems 1.8--1.9, proof recurrence, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize intrinsic inverse-Jacobian restrictions that are sufficient and close to necessary for uniform concentration of degree-bounded rational recovery.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pathwise denominator induction by a formula-independent smallest-singular-value bound for the covariance inverse map.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches found bow-free sufficient stability and an ill-conditioned four-node path, but no indegree-two rational-chart characterization tied to symbolic formula output.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say denominator and covariance-eigenvalue margins already guarantee stability.
seed_details.rebuttal: Those margins do not bound the inverse Jacobian or high-degree coefficient growth, and the published four-node construction separates identification from conditioning.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The chart restriction is intrinsic and the failure side must hold on a nondegenerate sequence, not at one singular law.

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 5 examples, computational study, proof of the HTC results, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Compute exact recursive-degree tables through the smallest non-tree cases with analytic witnesses for every attained degree.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Refine graph-level rational-identification enumeration to the rank-intersection closure over all original coordinates and all degrees below the first success.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Published censuses report identification classes and fibers, but not source-defined recursive formula degree.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may dismiss this as a finite computer-algebra catalogue.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds as a standalone paper, so the census is used only for falsification, base cases, and reproducible lower certificates.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: No flagship claim is attached to enumeration alone.

literature_map.settled: Bounded-degree adaptive Gröbner search is complete below a supplied cutoff; Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) on the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) on auxiliary cutsets, specializing to \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\); generic identification is decidable in polynomial space; inverse degrees can be bounded from Rees-algebra regularity under additional algebraic hypotheses.
literature_map.unoccupied: No source bounds \(ID_G\) uniformly over every rationally identifiable acyclic indegree-two graph, proves an explicit rationally identifiable family outside auxiliary cutsets, or supplies a locked-coordinate Hilbert-rank invariant stable under all recursive structural and disturbance adjunctions.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Hassanzadeh and Simis do not prove that SEM graph algebras are Cohen--Macaulay and give no recursive-order lower bound; Dörfler et al. return no rational inverse; the selected kernel is not subsumed.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Writing arc from Hollering, Misra, and Sturma; degree-by-degree certificate construction from their Corollary 4.5 and Theorem 5.1; their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 for the \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) HTC and IC bounds and Proposition 7.4 for the \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) AC bound as subclass background; Hilbert control of inverse maps from Hassanzadeh and Simis.

literature_map.settled: Directed-tree models reduce missing-edge constraints to two-scalar bilinear equations; identifying cycles yield at most quadratic ambiguity; Gupta and Bläser give the complete one, two, or infinite classification; Briefs and Bläser accelerate that same tree-only predicate.
literature_map.unoccupied: At indegree two a missing-edge equation can contain four structural coefficients, and no paper supplies a finite block-correspondence classification or constant-degree completeness theorem.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The first abstraction used by the complete tree proof fails before its Möbius and unicyclic arguments begin, so the target is not a routine extension.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Problem formulation from Gupta and Bläser; exact pair-elimination boundary from van der Zander et al.; bounded-degree falsification from Hollering, Misra, and Sturma.

literature_map.settled: Tree identification and fiber cardinality are complete, and transfer matrices provide constructive formulas; the faster algorithm changes runtime rather than the algebraic class.
literature_map.unoccupied: None of these papers minimizes certificate degree over all recursive orders including disturbance coordinates, so expression growth from one transfer product is not a lower bound.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The tree seed survives as a lower-bound laboratory but does not replace the chosen indegree-two frontier.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Pairwise resultant construction from van der Zander et al. and completeness decomposition from Gupta and Bläser.
